:::{#thm-vec-outer-product}
#### The vectorization of an outer product is a Kronecker product

For a vector $\vecf{u}$ with $m$ entries
and a vector $\vecf{v}$ with $n$ entries,
the [vectorization](#def-vectorization)
of the [outer product](#def-outer-product) $\oprod{\vecf{u}}{\vecf{v}}$
[equals](linear-algebra.qmd#def-matrix-equality) the [Kronecker product](#def-kronecker-product) $\vecf{v} \otimes \vecf{u}$:

$$
\underbrace{\vctf{\oprod{\vecf{u}}{\vecf{v}}}}_{mn \times 1}
= \underbrace{\vecf{v}}_{n \times 1} \otimes \underbrace{\vecf{u}}_{m \times 1}
$$

:::

::: proof

[Column](linear-algebra.qmd#def-matrix-column) $j$ of $\oprod{\vecf{u}}{\vecf{v}}$ has entries $u_1 v_j, \ldots, u_m v_j$,
so it is the vector $v_j \vecf{u}$.
Then

$$
\ba
\vctf{\oprod{\vecf{u}}{\vecf{v}}}
&= \begin{bmatrix} v_1 \vecf{u} \\ \vdots \\ v_n \vecf{u} \end{bmatrix}
&& \text{(definition of vectorization)}
\\
&= \vecf{v} \otimes \vecf{u}
&& \text{(definition of the Kronecker product, with one column of blocks)}
\ea
$$

:::
